subject.title: RFC: Distributed Agent Runtime — separate control plane from agent compute

question: Should OpenClaw pursue a first-class Gateway control-plane and per-agent runtime split in core, and which Phase 0/1 contract should be approved first?
rationale: The request changes core architecture, public config/protocol shape, runtime isolation, upgrade behavior, and security boundaries, so automation cannot safely choose the product contract or trust model.

options.title: Approve a narrow Phase 0/1 design
options.body: Keep embedded mode as the default and first specify per-agent lifecycle plus local process/runtime protocol boundaries before container or Kubernetes execution.

options.title: Defer to backend placement work
options.body: Leave this RFC as context while maintainers review the narrower subagent execution backend/profile tracker and its open implementation PRs first.

options.title: Pause the core runtime split
options.body: Do not sponsor distributed runtime core work until current gateway stability and setup priorities are further along.

recommendation.title: Approve a narrow Phase 0/1 design
recommendation.body: Keep embedded mode as the default and first specify per-agent lifecycle plus local process/runtime protocol boundaries before container or Kubernetes execution.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest recent history across Gateway/runtime seams and authored the open worker-runtime isolation experiment.
